Affiliation

Published

2026/08/19

BDC334 · Undergraduate

Biogeography & Global Ecology

Study how biodiversity is distributed across space, why communities differ, how gradients structure ecosystems, and how quantitative evidence moves us from description to explanation.

Start with the course overview Begin Lab 1

Focus

Patterns, processes, and ecological gradients

Approach

Lectures, worked examples, and data-led practicals

Tools

Ecological datasets, spreadsheets, and R

  • Describe biodiversity patterns across spatial scales.
  • Explain how environmental gradients structure ecological communities.
  • Interpret species and environmental data using appropriate quantitative tools.
  • Connect multivariate patterns to ecological mechanisms and limitations.

Follow the course

01

Read the overview

Use the course overview to orient yourself to the module structure and expectations.

02

Work through the lectures

Move from ecological scale and ecosystems to gradients, biodiversity, and unified explanations.

03

Apply the ideas

Use the practicals to inspect real ecological data, calculate distances, and quantify biodiversity patterns.

Start each practical with the linked data files and instructions on that page. Keep your working spreadsheet or R project organised so that the raw data remain unchanged.
